title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 23
paragraphs: The Athenians, seeing the cavalry riding against them no longer by squadrons but all together, shouted to the rest of the army to come help. While the whole body of foot-soldiers was coming to their aid, a sharp fight arose over the body. As long as the three hundred were alone they had much the worse of it and were about to abandon the body; but when the mass of the army came to their aid, then the horsemen could no longer sustain the fight, nor did they succeed in recovering the body; and besides him they lost others of their number too. They then drew off about two furlongs away and deliberated what to do; and it seemed best to them, having no commander, to ride back to Mardonius.
